# Continuous Stage A cohort

This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
prepared environment each
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
go/no-go between blocks.

This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
in the order the tools require, up to the
owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
it. The one-task first block keeps its own
[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).

## What the harness enforces

- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
  launcher holds it.
- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
  before reservation. Serial
  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
  Claude admission and image qualification alike
  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
  `agent`, ahead of them.
  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
  ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
  The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
  execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).

deadline, output controls and one-attempt policy. #161 delivers the native adapter
and #163 delivers its controlled-research binding; fresh admission must still prove
the exact effective runtime before #50 may create a live v5 freeze. The checked-in
v5 fixtures are synthetic only.

### [pi-coding-agent-setup #315/#321](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/pi-coding-agent-setup/issues/315) — RelayView integration/export evidence

Preserve production-owner workload, local identity, resource, terminal-candidate
and paired-checkpoint evidence. These cards feed eval #64/#65 and Stage B only;
they do not execute or report another comparative cohort.

## Phase gates and tracker dependencies

An arrow means “consumes the named stage artifact.” #24, #25 and #50 span both
stages, so their Stage A artifact gates cannot be represented as dependencies on
those issues closing: doing so would create a Stage A/Stage B cycle. Native tracker
dependencies retain only whole-issue implementation prerequisites; the following
stage transitions are enforced by immutable artifact identities and acceptance
checks in the issue bodies.

- Stage A freeze: #50 → seven-arm conformance, accepted #112/#116 legacy-six
  evidence and fresh Claude Code `github-excluded-v1` delivery/admission.
  #73/#98–#102 remain historical inputs.
- Stage A execution: #24 → #23, Stage A #50 freeze and all-seven admission.
- Stage A publication: #25 → Stage A #24 seal.
- Stage B freeze: #50 → Stage A #25 disposition, #64/#68/#172 operational evidence
  and standard Pi #130 admission.
- Stage B execution: #24 → #23, Stage B #50 freeze, #68/#172 and Pi #130.
- Stage B analysis: #66 → Stage B #24 seal.
- Stage B publication: #25 → Stage B #24 seal and #66.

Offline-study work may consume the final expansion completion identity but must not
become a benchmark prerequisite. Historical #63/#69/#89 and completed cross-repo
cards are reconciled by ADR-0010 comments without rewriting their closed evidence.

## Approved additions (2026-09-09)

- The implemented prospective [task outcome v2 contract](task-outcomes-v2.md)
  fulfills #131 by separating verifier observation, termination, delivery, primary
  task score and automated/human dispositions. Eligible timeout remains primary zero.
- [#128](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/128)
  supplies the prospective v4 schema/validator/fixtures and complete effective
  freeze boundary. #50 still supplies each real numerical freeze. Historical
  v2/v3 artifacts are not relabeled.
- [#129](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/129)
  specifies standard Pi capabilities; [#130](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/130)
  implements and admits that single-agent arm for Stage B only.
- [#132](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/132)
  owns a separate later RelayView-only feature-ablation study, consuming
  [RelayView #446](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/pi-coding-agent-setup/issues/446).
  Neither this child nor completion of its entire parent epic gates the baseline.

## Seven-arm amendment (2026-09-14)

- [#160](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/160)
  supplies the prospective v5 contract/schema/validator, deterministic seven-arm
  fixtures and the exact Claude Code subscription baseline. It does not mutate or
  relabel v1–v4 evidence and does not claim live Claude delivery or admission.
- Stage A applies the unchanged
  `resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1` futility rule independently
  to all seven arms. Stage B is every survivor plus RelayView Sol, RelayView local
  and Pi, for three through ten arms.

#50 also owns inherited-evaluator integration controls (base/gold, upstream parity,
rebuild/test discovery, typed setup/parser failure and tamper cases), prospective
repository-disjointness/exposure disclosure, and actual resource/control evidence.
#23/#24 enforce finite execution windows and reconcile every scheduled slot.
#25/#66 report paired task-level uncertainty, failures, unknowns, source restrictions
and small-sample limitations; checkpoints are not causal feature ablations.

The purpose is honest comparison of recognizable developer configurations.
Preserve native competitor capabilities; do not transplant RelayView-specific memory,
AST/LSP enhancements, expert or multi-role/review machinery for parity. Disclose
the shared-broker/GitHub-excluded modifications rather than claiming untouched
stock behavior. Separately demonstrate governance and human-review value.

---
status: accepted
date: 2026-10-03
---

> Amended: [ADR-0029](0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md) adopts the
> release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the same 23 tasks, validators and order with
> a prepared environment for each, in place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`.

# Screen Stage A on the 23 reviewed archive tasks

Stage A screens the seven standard arms on the 23 tasks in the reviewed subset
of the full `multilang-task-archive` release, with one repetition and one
attempt per slot: 161 scheduled slots. Independent review left two of the 25
selected tasks `unresolved`, and both are dropped without replacement:

| Task | Language | Review decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` | C | Archive issue #15, PR #55, 2026-09-29: `original-v1` scores a partial `tonemap`/`combine` candidate 1; the proposed `metadata-flags-v1` correction was not adopted. |
| `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180` | Rust | Archive issue #20, PR #60, 2026-10-02: `original-v1` accepts an incomplete Context Contents UI candidate and rejects a credible alternative for omitting a reference-authored test name. |

The corpus is bound to the reviewed archive release: its tag, release ID,
manifest SHA-256 and archive commit, plus each task's complete archive binding.
No dataset corpus file is created for it. The release is pinned at or after
archive commit `1c5a58f8b0227b5cfa1be85542493af90c6caab7`, whose grader view
carries the selected test patch as `validation/tests.patch`. #219 verifies the
release's harness adoption one task at a time: for each of the 23 bindings,
`task_archive.inspect` and production `admit` must pass. Consuming the release
as one multi-task release is a separate harness capability.

The 23 retained tasks keep their v3 task IDs, source revisions, task text and
repositories. Each is graded by the validator its archive review selected. The
executable allocation is `c=2`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`, `js=3`, `rust=2`, `java=0`,
`ts=4`, `cs=4` across 23 distinct repositories. The oldest retained
`created_at` is `2026-04-03T09:27:24Z` (`gfx-rs__wgpu-9367`), unchanged from
v3. Reports disclose the reduced C and Rust strata alongside the absence of
Java.

Slot counts derive from the frozen corpus: tasks × the seven standard arms ×
one repetition. Validators, preflight receipts, launchers, audits, seals and
the `stage-a-capability-disposition/1` artifact compare against that derived
value, never a literal. For this corpus the disposition holds 161 records,
23 per arm.

The futility gate is unchanged as an absolute rule. An arm is
capability-futile only when `resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1`
after all 23 of its slots reconcile; an arm whose upper bound is at least 2/23
survives. One task is 1/23 of an arm's denominator, about 4.35 percentage
points, and reports say so.

The cohort runs every scheduled block in order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze. Approval of
that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no first-block stop, no
`first_block_task_id`, no first-block gate and no owner go/no-go between
blocks.

Each block runs under the existing per-block supervisor watchdog
(`SUPERVISOR_POLICY` in `stage_a_execution.py`); no runtime is sized for the
whole cohort. When a block completes cleanly, the launcher starts the next
block from the same ledger under the same admitted supervisor policy, with no
operator action. A block that does not complete cleanly, including a watchdog
stop, stops the cohort fail-closed for diagnosis. An uncertain or active
attempt is never replayed. The ledger is never reset. An infrastructure stop
retains the ledger and evidence. Resuming the same ledger requires the same
admitted configuration and is a recovery, not a new approval.

Authenticated Claude enrollment renewal during the run is a recorded operator
recovery, not an owner go/no-go. It follows the pre-launch recovery in the
[first-block gate runbook](../../runbooks/stage-a-first-block-gate.md). A
renewal:

- keeps the same account, token, tier and credit/isolation settings;
- authenticates against the frozen identities;
- carries a new recorded account-policy confirmation;
- never extends or overwrites the original receipt;
- adds no reservation or refund;
- is bound into the ledger and evidence.

Without a valid renewal, a pending Claude turn that the current receipt cannot
cover fails closed before reservation. A renewal with a changed identity is
rejected.

After every slot is terminal or explicitly unstarted, an offline audit covers
all 161 slots, including each renewal's chronology, and #24 seals the cohort.

`stephenberry__glaze-2731` is one of the 23 and runs as fresh slots. The #155
and #220 Glaze blocks, with their first-block stops, audits and owner
decisions, remain separately reported historical evidence. Neither becomes a
prefix, a slot or a result of the new ledger.

The exclusion is outcome-independent. Both dispositions are task-validator
review findings judged against task-visible requirements with constructed
review candidates, and no comparative trial has run on either task. The
libavif review states that its candidates were written for the review, not
taken from a task-solving agent attempt. Glaze is the only task with
comparative outcomes, and it is retained. Dropping rather than replacing
follows the v5 replacement rule: replacement is allowed only for a validation
failure found before any comparative outcome, and never after the first trial
begins. Stage A trials began with the #155 block, and a replacement would also
need its own archive import and review. A proportional futility threshold
would round to zero or one possible resolution at this size and would change
the rule after outcomes from one task are known. Two audited Glaze blocks have
exercised the launch path, including archive-bound grading; fail-closed
recovery rules, not further approvals, protect the remaining blocks.

## Consequences

- This supersedes the 25-task and 175-slot counts in
  [ADR-0010](0010-stage-multilang-screening-before-expansion.md) and
  [ADR-0012](0012-add-claude-code-to-staged-multilang.md), the C and Rust
  strata of [ADR-0015](0015-record-stage-a-successor-corpus-allocation.md),
  and the "ordinary 25-task Stage A contract" in
  [ADR-0014](0014-scope-archive-first-block-execution.md). ADR-0014's one-task
  first-block scope remains valid for its own freezes. The
  [v5 contract](../../contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md) carries the
  amended passages. The seven standard arms, one repetition, the absolute
  gate, the separate Stage B freeze and the no-pooling rule remain in force.
- The `swe-bench-live-multilang-stage-a-v3` corpus, its manifest digest
  `sha256:9dfb019c4f81e4ac4dd64a252e6ffe0ce08bc3be9238d37e656808f308f8072b`,
  and every earlier freeze, ledger, approval, audit, seal and receipt stay
  unchanged.
- The full release's adoption record names exactly the 23 eligible tasks and
  records the two exclusions with their review evidence.
- #24 prepares the Stage A freeze from that adoption record and owns Stage A
  seal accounting. #50 owns only the Stage B freeze.
- Executable enforcement is not implemented yet and is pending
  [#229](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/229). That covers derived slot counts, the multi-task
  archive scope, the continuous run with automatic advance, enrollment
  renewal, and the full-cohort audit and seal. Until it lands, the harness
  accepts only 25-task freezes on the historical dataset path and the one-task
  `archive-first-block/1` scope, so a 23-task freeze cannot validate.
- A new freeze also needs a reviewed result-root retention procedure for task
  source and workspace trees
  ([#230](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/230)). It is exercised provider-free against all 23
  release task sources, without weakening the global secret scanner.
- This decision grants no execution approval. Fresh admission, a reconciled
  research and provider capacity plan, the numerical freeze and owner approval
  of that freeze remain separate.

## Alternatives considered

- Replace each dropped task with the next same-language repository. Rejected:
  barred after the first trial, and it would add unreviewed tasks.
- Keep both tasks under `original-v1`. Rejected: review showed each validator
  accepts an incorrect candidate, and lean-ctx's also rejects a credible one.
- Adopt the exploratory corrections. Rejected by the owner reviews.
- Scale the futility threshold to the smaller corpus. Rejected: the gate is
  absolute by design.
- Keep a first-block stop and continuation go/no-go. Rejected: the launch path
  is already audited, and fail-closed recovery covers later blocks.
- Size one supervised runtime for the whole cohort. Rejected: per-block
  watchdogs keep each failure bounded.
- Treat enrollment expiry as an owner go/no-go. Rejected: an
  identity-preserving renewal is an operator recovery.
- Write a 23-task dataset corpus file. Rejected: archive tasks never fall back
  to dataset rows.

## Decision evidence

- Archive manifest at `multilang-task-archive` `a64c16b`: 25 tasks, 23 in the
  reviewed subset (20 `verified-corrected`, 3 `verified-unchanged`,
  2 `unresolved`). `manifest.json` is unchanged at `1c5a58f`.
- `tasks/AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300/review/assessment.md` and
  `tasks/yvgude__lean-ctx-1180/review/assessment.md` in that archive.
- [Post-Glaze #24 handoff](../../historical/issue-notes/24/post-glaze-handoff-2026-09-29.md):
  175 slots apply only if all 25 tasks remain eligible, and the Glaze block is
  never a prefix of a new ledger.

# Continuous Stage A cohort

This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
prepared environment each
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
go/no-go between blocks.

This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
in the order the tools require, up to the
owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
it. The one-task first block keeps its own
[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).

## What the harness enforces

- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
  launcher holds it.
- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
  before reservation. Serial
  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
  Claude admission and image qualification alike
  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
  `agent`, ahead of them.
  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
  ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
  The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
  execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).

## Conserved Claude subscription accounting

`claude-capacity-ledger/1` implements the #167 owner-approved Max 5x assumptions:
3 session percentage points and 1 weekly percentage point per whole attempt,
two workflow units held back, concurrency one, no credits or paid overflow,
and evaluation-only usage. The historical 12%/2% example yields 29/98 workflow
units before the two-unit holdback; it is never a live reading.

Observations contain both exposed windows, their epoch IDs and reset times,
nonsecret evidence digests, and explicit account/restriction fields. Missing or
stale readings, a provider restriction, outside usage, a changed tier, credits,
or an unaccounted newly exposed cap reject dispatch. A reading expires after
300 seconds or at the first reset boundary, whichever occurs first. Missing
Opus-only telemetry remains the specific owner-accepted exception.

Each epoch conserves a baseline and consumed workflow units. Refreshing a low
rounded percentage cannot replenish spent units. A changed epoch needs a
separate confirmation digest after the previous reset boundary. Only that
window is rebaselined. Active leases carry a conservative whole-workflow charge
into a new epoch; the other window keeps its consumption. Finishing, failing,
timing out or restarting a workflow never refunds its charge.

The numerical policy embeds the pre-freeze qualification journal. The scheduler
retains that exact prefix and rejects changed qualification history, missing or
duplicated attempt charges, mismatched quota snapshots and earlier accounting
versions. Numerical v5 freezes use `stage-scheduler-state/2`; historical v4/v5
fixtures without the extension retain their original state format.

Provider and shared-research workflow reservations are created in the same
scheduler transaction. An exhausted research account cannot leave a Claude-only
lease behind. Claude's epoch balances already include charged reservations;
the generic scheduler subtracts the two-unit holdback once. Deferrals stay in
the current seven-slot block, and the fixed cohort end reconciles pending slots
as unstarted. No capability failure or eligible timeout gains a retry.

Schedule an immutable `stage_id` and exact frozen arm set. Screening blocks contain
the seven standard arms. Expansion blocks contain the surviving standard arms plus
both RelayView arms and standard Pi, and therefore contain three through ten arms. Retain seeded
task/repetition blocks, reservations, quota evidence, stable IDs, bounded retries,
reconciliation and digest-checked resume. Reject missing, duplicate or extra arms
and any attempt to mix stage, corpus, policy or seal identity.

### [agent-harness-evals #24](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/24) — Execute and seal both stages

Execute Stage A only after its #50 freeze, #23 scheduler and all-seven standard-arm
admission. Seal every scheduled slot and stop for #25's report/disposition. Later,
execute Stage B only after a new #50 freeze and RelayView/Pi/selected-arm admission.
Retain terminal and applicable RelayView checkpoint evidence, prove quiescence and
hidden-score isolation, and emit a distinct immutable seal for each stage.

### [agent-harness-evals #25](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/25) — Publish screening and expansion reports

First publish every Stage A arm, denominator, per-task outcome, all-scheduled bound,
uncertainty, time/resource evidence and futility disposition. Do not force culling
or infer a precise rank. Later publish Stage B separately, disclose adaptive arm
selection and consume #66's Stage B secondary analysis. Never pool stages. The
screening report can complete without #66; the issue remains the owner of the final
expansion publication.

### [agent-harness-evals #50](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/50) — Freeze both MultiLang corpora and resources

For Stage A, independently verify and pin the candidate MultiLang revision
`62dc0745c40f067fc366ae3eb1a26136e5928f85`, `created_at` semantics and source
timestamps. Freeze 25 tasks dated on/after 2026-04-01 with `c=3`, `cpp=3`,
`go=3`, `js=3`, `rust=3`, `java=2`, `ts=4`, `cs=4`, from exactly 25
repositories. After validation,
select newest-per-repository tasks within each language by `created_at` descending
and bytewise `instance_id` ascending. Freeze the remaining same-language order for
pre-outcome validation-only replacement. Verify the projected raw-data cutoff
`2026-04-16T18:19:25Z` and publish the final post-validation cutoff. Deliver and validate the MultiLang adapter,
root discovery, per-task commands/parser, compiled-language resource envelope,
image digests, verifier isolation and typed outcomes. Freeze screening arm,
research, deadline, attempt, exactly-one-repetition and resource policies before
outcomes. Any later study of multiple tries is a separately identified cohort
with its own aggregation and interpretation policy.
The Stage A research freeze consumes #112: every legacy standard arm must bind the
effective `github-excluded-v1` policy and accepted #116 live admission, and Claude
Code must bind its separate fresh exact-identity admission. The freeze
rejects default `public-web-v1`, native Codex/Sol search, stale #73/#98-#102
admission and any requested/effective policy mismatch.

After Stage A is completely sealed and reported, freeze a disjoint Stage B corpus,
exact surviving standard arms plus both RelayView arms and standard Pi, sample size, practical
thresholds and resources before expansion outcomes. The Stage A report may inform
prospective sizing; task outcomes may not select expansion tasks. No unresolved
measurement or execution choice may pass either freeze.

Coordinate #64, #65 and #66 for Stage B without blocking Stage A. RelayView joins
only the disjoint expansion cohort. Preserve #315/#321 operational/export evidence
as prerequisites rather than duplicate comparative execution.

### [agent-harness-evals #64](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/64) — Production RelayView adapter

Retain terminal and paired-checkpoint, isolation, lifecycle, deadline, budget and
scoring requirements. Consume the successor MultiLang measurement/outcome boundary for Stage B.
This delivery can proceed while Stage A runs but is not a screening prerequisite.

### [agent-harness-evals #65](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/65) — Admit both RelayView arms

Perform fresh exact-pair admission against the Stage B contract and MultiLang
measurement boundary. Retain exact role/model/provider/local-checkpoint/research
and shared-account evidence. This gates Stage B only.

### [agent-harness-evals #66](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/66) — Analyze RelayView checkpoints

Consume only the Stage B seal. Report the predeclared paired initial/reviewed/
terminal analyses, missingness, uncertainty, time and resources. Do not use Stage A
as anchors and do not pool it into RelayView estimates. Supply #25's expansion
report; do not block the screening report.

### [agent-harness-evals #68](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/68) — Research readiness

Treat readiness as stage-specific. Fresh declared research admission for the seven
standard arms gates Stage A. RelayView research assembly and admission gate Stage B.
For Stage A, #112–#116 replace native Codex/Sol search with the shared controlled
researcher and require `github-excluded-v1` for the legacy six arms; #160 freezes
the same policy through the Claude Code MCP pair, which still requires fresh admission. The default remains
`public-web-v1` outside benchmark invocations. No semantic or new multi-source
prerequisite is introduced.

### [agent-harness-evals #70–#73](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/70) — Completed research delivery

Preserve the closed implementation/admission evidence and shared budget-v2 rules.
They supplied #98–#102's historical public-web qualifications; current Stage A
admission comes from #116 and its six children. Old results are not relabeled as
MultiLang outcomes or current admission.

### [agent-harness-evals #98–#102](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/98) — Fresh standard-arm qualification

Preserve these completed five-project qualifications as public-web operational
evidence under their recorded profiles. They are not `github-excluded-v1`
admission and must not be relabeled or pooled. Scores cannot select screening
tasks or support capability ranking.

### [agent-harness-evals #112–#116](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/112) — GitHub-excluded Stage A research

boundary; #114 delivers the opt-in broker enforcement and pinned release; #115
routes all six standard arms through it while preserving normal public-web
defaults; #116 performs fresh exact-arm live admission for those six. All four
children gate the legacy-six portion of Stage A; the Claude arm has an additional

deadline, output controls and one-attempt policy. #161 delivers the native adapter
and #163 delivers its controlled-research binding; fresh admission must still prove
the exact effective runtime before #50 may create a live v5 freeze. The checked-in
v5 fixtures are synthetic only.

Preserve production-owner workload, local identity, resource, terminal-candidate

An arrow means “consumes the named stage artifact.” #24, #25 and #50 span both
stages, so their Stage A artifact gates cannot be represented as dependencies on

stage transitions are enforced by immutable artifact identities and acceptance

- Stage A execution: #24 → #23, Stage A #50 freeze and all-seven admission.
- Stage A publication: #25 → Stage A #24 seal.

- Stage B execution: #24 → #23, Stage B #50 freeze, #68/#172 and Pi #130.

Offline-study work may consume the final expansion completion identity but must not
become a benchmark prerequisite. Historical #63/#69/#89 and completed cross-repo
cards are reconciled by ADR-0010 comments without rewriting their closed evidence.

- The implemented prospective [task outcome v2 contract](task-outcomes-v2.md)
  fulfills #131 by separating verifier observation, termination, delivery, primary
  task score and automated/human dispositions. Eligible timeout remains primary zero.
- [#128](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/128)
  supplies the prospective v4 schema/validator/fixtures and complete effective
  freeze boundary. #50 still supplies each real numerical freeze. Historical

## Seven-arm amendment (2026-09-14)

  supplies the prospective v5 contract/schema/validator, deterministic seven-arm

#50 also owns inherited-evaluator integration controls (base/gold, upstream parity,

stock behavior. Separately demonstrate governance and human-review value.

# Run agents in prepared environments, keeping their declared dependency paths

## Context

A Stage A agent works offline, as the unprivileged agent user
([ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)), in its task
image's `/testbed` after repository sanitization. Sanitization rebuilds Git
from the base commit and runs `git clean -ffdx`, which removes every ignored
dependency folder inside the repository, such as `node_modules`. The agent
cannot read the caches and toolchains the image keeps under a mode-0700
`/root`. So in the agent's workspace most tasks could not build their own
code offline. Cohort attempt 9 (#24) showed both effects:

- surveyjs's offline `npm install` outlived its in-place build's 6,467-second
  share and stopped image qualification;
- 12 of the 18 tasks that qualified had grader builds that exited nonzero as
  the agent.

The owner decided (2026-10-11, multilang-task-archive #76) that dependencies
are prepared ahead of time and belong to each task's environment, for agents
and qualification alike. The archive's ADR 0011 records each task's
**prepared environment**. It is a second owned image derived from the image
the task's selected validator grades in. Its caches and toolchains are moved
out of `/root`, its offline configuration is in the image's `Env`, and its
dependency folders inside the repository are **declared dependency paths**.
Each declared path is recorded with the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of its
`_filesystem_entries` inventory, the same entry shape and order as this
repository's sanitizer. Graders never run in a prepared environment.

The sanitizer `swe_bench_workspace.py` (contract `swe-bench-repository-v1`) is
pinned by its SHA-256 in frozen instruments:

- the MultiLang v1 to v3 corpora and their sanitizer runner bundle;
- the control-reuse and successor reproducibility checks;
- the SWE-bench Verified task manifest.

A one-byte change to it fails 10 tests that pass on `main`, and leaves the
frozen v3 corpus unexecutable. [ADR 0021](0021-exclude-untracked-build-products-from-stage-a-candidates.md)
kept it unchanged for the same reason.

## Decision

**The agent's image is the prepared environment.** An archive task's agent
sandbox and its image qualification run in the artifact that
`environment.prepared.artifact_id` names. It is restored offline from the
owner store, like the grader's image. Graders keep the image their validator
names (the binding's `image_digest`). The binding's `environment_digest` pins
the prepared environment, and `task_archive.prepared_environment` accepts it
only if all of these hold:

- the artifact is neither the primary nor any validator's;
- its definition names the bound grader image as its base and this artifact
  as the prepared one;
- its declared paths are the definition's.

The selection carries the agent's image (`agent_image`) and the declared paths
beside the grader's image, and `validate_selection` re-derives both.

**One lifecycle holds both images.** `TaskImageStore.prepare` loads the
grader's image, then the agent's, and records both. `check` serves either, and
`release` removes the agent's image first, since it extends the grader's
layers. The grader's image stays loaded while the agent's converts and loads.
So the Docker store needs the larger of the grader's preparation and the
grader's expanded bound plus the agent image's preparation. Conversion stages
one image at a time, so the staging filesystem needs only the larger single
preparation. The release image size record `task-archive-image-sizes/2`
measures each task's agent image beside its grader's. The configuration
carries each agent image's `agent_expanded_upper_bytes`, which `validate_plan`
requires to be the record's estimate. Doctor sizes the store and staging this
way.

**Sanitizer contract v2 keeps exactly the declared paths.** The Stage A
sanitizer is `stage_a_workspace.py`, contract `swe-bench-repository-v2`. It
runs in the sandbox beside an unchanged copy of `swe_bench_workspace.py` and
imports its helpers, so no frozen pin moves. Its identity hashes both files.
It runs v1's steps, with these changes:

- **Refusals, before anything changes.** Each declared path must be
  repository-relative and canonical, with no `.`, `..` or `.git` part. It must
  not be tracked, hold tracked files, be nested in another declared path or
  overlap a runtime mount, and it must sit directly in a tracked directory or
  at the root.
- **The clean keeps them.** `git clean -ffdx` excludes each declared path, as
  it excludes the image's empty runtime mountpoints. Every other ignored or
  untracked file is still removed.
- **Each is checked against its hash.** Once the workspace is final, each
  declared path must be a real directory whose inventory hash equals its
  recorded one. A missing or changed path fails sanitization by name:
  `declared dependency path differs from its recorded hash: <path>`.
- **The boundary admits them whole.** The workspace boundary admits each
  declared path without listing its content, which the hash check covers.
- **The evidence records them.** The evidence lists the kept paths as
  `dependency_paths` and carries the v2 identity, which Stage A's workspace
  preparation requires.

The SWE-bench Verified path, the MultiLang verifier and the frozen corpora keep
v1.

**A declared path is environment, never candidate.** Nothing in it is ever
part of a patch:

- Stage A capture's staging program never stages it. It also unstages
  whatever the agent staged or committed inside it, whether or not the
  repository ignores the folder.
- The archive's host-side capture excludes it from its intent-to-add and its
  diff.
- The Claude adapter leaves it out of its baseline snapshot and its own
  candidate export. Qualification's timing of those steps leaves it out too.

**Adoption.** Stage A adopts the archive release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` in
place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, under
[ADR 0016](0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)'s binding rule. It
holds the same 23 tasks, validators and order. Its bindings differ only in the
archive commit and manifest, each task's metadata hash and its environment
digest, because each task now declares a prepared environment. Every task has
one; six declare dependency paths:

| Task | Declared paths |
| --- | --- |
| defuddle, playcanvas, NotionNext | `node_modules` |
| manifest | 3 |
| surveyjs | 6 |
| mui-x | 32 |

The release record is [stage-a-prepared-23-v1](../../releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.md).

## Consequences

- An agent starts with its task's dependencies installed and readable, as on
  a developer's machine. It can build and test offline without reinstalling.
- The agent's environment differs from the grader's only by the prepared
  dependencies and configuration. Grades, validators and review evidence stand.
- Sanitizing a prepared workspace hashes every declared file once. In the real
  prepared images, offline, it took 5.3 s for manifest's 3 paths, 17.9 s for
  surveyjs's 6 and 32.9 s for mui-x's 32, well inside the setup phase. Exactly
  the declared paths remained in each.
- Preparing a task loads two images. Doctor's store requirement for the
  largest task grows by about that task's expanded image. The staging
  requirement grows only by the agent image's own preparation.
- An agent's change inside a declared path, such as a patched dependency, is
  never graded.
- Every arm runs in a new environment and sandbox implementation. The
  execution host, every arm's admission, image qualification and the freeze
  are redone at the new commit, as [ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md#re-admission-and-freeze)
  describes for a sandbox change.
- Known limits carried, not fixed:
  - **surveyjs.** Its grader's test command names root's Chrome path, which
    the agent cannot reach. The prepared image's `CHROME_BIN` names the moved
    browser.
  - **wgpu.** Its tests need the untracked `.gpuconfig` that sanitization
    removes. An agent can regenerate it with `cargo xtask test`.

`_filesystem_entries` inventory, the same entry shape and order as this
repository's sanitizer. Graders never run in a prepared environment.

The sanitizer `swe_bench_workspace.py` (contract `swe-bench-repository-v1`) is
pinned by its SHA-256 in frozen instruments:

- the MultiLang v1 to v3 corpora and their sanitizer runner bundle;
- the control-reuse and successor reproducibility checks;
- the SWE-bench Verified task manifest.

A one-byte change to it fails 10 tests that pass on `main`, and leaves the
frozen v3 corpus unexecutable. [ADR 0021](0021-exclude-untracked-build-products-from-stage-a-candidates.md)
kept it unchanged for the same reason.

## Decision

**The agent's image is the prepared environment.** An archive task's agent
sandbox and its image qualification run in the artifact that
`environment.prepared.artifact_id` names. It is restored offline from the
owner store, like the grader's image. Graders keep the image their validator
names (the binding's `image_digest`). The binding's `environment_digest` pins
the prepared environment, and `task_archive.prepared_environment` accepts it
only if all of these hold:

- the artifact is neither the primary nor any validator's;
- its definition names the bound grader image as its base and this artifact
  as the prepared one;
- its declared paths are the definition's.

The selection carries the agent's image (`agent_image`) and the declared paths
beside the grader's image, and `validate_selection` re-derives both.

**One lifecycle holds both images.** `TaskImageStore.prepare` loads the
grader's image, then the agent's, and records both. `check` serves either, and
`release` removes the agent's image first, since it extends the grader's
layers. The grader's image stays loaded while the agent's converts and loads.
So the Docker store needs the larger of the grader's preparation and the
grader's expanded bound plus the agent image's preparation. Conversion stages
one image at a time, so the staging filesystem needs only the larger single
preparation. The release image size record `task-archive-image-sizes/2`
measures each task's agent image beside its grader's. The configuration
carries each agent image's `agent_expanded_upper_bytes`, which `validate_plan`
requires to be the record's estimate. Doctor sizes the store and staging this
way.

**Sanitizer contract v2 keeps exactly the declared paths.** The Stage A
sanitizer is `stage_a_workspace.py`, contract `swe-bench-repository-v2`. It
runs in the sandbox beside an unchanged copy of `swe_bench_workspace.py` and
imports its helpers, so no frozen pin moves. Its identity hashes both files.
It runs v1's steps, with these changes:

- **Refusals, before anything changes.** Each declared path must be
  repository-relative and canonical, with no `.`, `..` or `.git` part. It must
  not be tracked, hold tracked files, be nested in another declared path or
  overlap a runtime mount, and it must sit directly in a tracked directory or
  at the root.
- **The clean keeps them.** `git clean -ffdx` excludes each declared path, as
  it excludes the image's empty runtime mountpoints. Every other ignored or
  untracked file is still removed.
- **Each is checked against its hash.** Once the workspace is final, each
  declared path must be a real directory whose inventory hash equals its
  recorded one. A missing or changed path fails sanitization by name:
  `declared dependency path differs from its recorded hash: <path>`.
- **The boundary admits them whole.** The workspace boundary admits each
  declared path without listing its content, which the hash check covers.
- **The evidence records them.** The evidence lists the kept paths as
  `dependency_paths` and carries the v2 identity, which Stage A's workspace
  preparation requires.

The SWE-bench Verified path, the MultiLang verifier and the frozen corpora keep
v1.

**A declared path is environment, never candidate.** Nothing in it is ever
part of a patch:

- Stage A capture's staging program never stages it. It also unstages
  whatever the agent staged or committed inside it, whether or not the
  repository ignores the folder.
- The archive's host-side capture excludes it from its intent-to-add and its
  diff.
- The Claude adapter leaves it out of its baseline snapshot and its own
  candidate export. Qualification's timing of those steps leaves it out too.

**Adoption.** Stage A adopts the archive release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` in
place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, under
[ADR 0016](0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)'s binding rule. It
holds the same 23 tasks, validators and order. Its bindings differ only in the
archive commit and manifest, each task's metadata hash and its environment
digest, because each task now declares a prepared environment. Every task has
one; six declare dependency paths:

| Task | Declared paths |
| --- | --- |
| defuddle, playcanvas, NotionNext | `node_modules` |
| manifest | 3 |
| surveyjs | 6 |
| mui-x | 32 |

The release record is [stage-a-prepared-23-v1](../../releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.md).

## Consequences

- An agent starts with its task's dependencies installed and readable, as on
  a developer's machine. It can build and test offline without reinstalling.
- The agent's environment differs from the grader's only by the prepared
  dependencies and configuration. Grades, validators and review evidence stand.
- Sanitizing a prepared workspace hashes every declared file once. In the real
  prepared images, offline, it took 5.3 s for manifest's 3 paths, 17.9 s for
  surveyjs's 6 and 32.9 s for mui-x's 32, well inside the setup phase. Exactly
  the declared paths remained in each.
- Preparing a task loads two images. Doctor's store requirement for the
  largest task grows by about that task's expanded image. The staging
  requirement grows only by the agent image's own preparation.
- An agent's change inside a declared path, such as a patched dependency, is
  never graded.
- Every arm runs in a new environment and sandbox implementation. The
  execution host, every arm's admission, image qualification and the freeze
  are redone at the new commit, as [ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md#re-admission-and-freeze)
  describes for a sandbox change.
- Known limits carried, not fixed:
  - **surveyjs.** Its grader's test command names root's Chrome path, which
    the agent cannot reach. The prepared image's `CHROME_BIN` names the moved
    browser.
  - **wgpu.** Its tests need the untracked `.gpuconfig` that sanitization
    removes. An agent can regenerate it with `cargo xtask test`.

# Unattended cohort execution: the attempt-3 stop and its fixes

## Status

Implemented in the harness for #271. The provider-free on-host rehearsal
result is recorded below. Attempt 3 is retired and attempt 4 is prepared only
after this change merges and asrock is re-admitted at its commit.

## The stop

Cohort attempt 3 on `cachyos-asrock` used freeze
`sha256:735f29e099a98b88ac982c891f9516ebaa50be6617c643aa06683363ff2e889b`,
which binds the admitted host profile
`sha256:5d890be13e19e9076558d4927af4c49704ad7d84a3b81b426d375cd55b4315e9` at
commit `97d18ae`. It launched at 2026-10-06T17:03:35Z as the supervised unit
`agent-evals-host-2976c9f832a744e048e913ff`.

- **The stop.** The unit stopped at 17:34:56Z on its first slot,
  `opencode-glm-5.3` × `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367`. The worker resolved the Z.AI key
  through `vault_session.unlock`, whose `getpass` raised `GetPassWarning`,
  because a systemd unit has no terminal.
- **What the ledger holds.** The reservation had been committed eleven seconds
  earlier. The ledger now holds one `in_flight` slot and 160 `pending`, and
  the attempt directory holds only `intent.json` and `interrupted.json`.
- **No requests were made.** The research sidecar and the agent container
  start after credential delivery, so no provider or research request was
  made.
- **Evidence retained.**
  - On the host: the unit journal and unit state, beside the attempt directory.
  - Off host: `cohort-attempt-3-launch-1-stop/evidence.tar`,
    `sha256:c13ee9a05ae8bbdfc891387f7cc0da780f552c784b6ee85ac504d51796e9ae43`.

## Why tests did not catch it

No test had run the live worker's credential path in a process without a
terminal:

- the execution tests replace `run_native`;
- the vault tests replace `getpass`;
- the runbook test's interpreter shim reported `isatty()` as true for every
  command, including the one its stand-in `systemd-run` started.

A read-only audit of the live path found these further defects, which would
have stopped or corrupted the cohort later:

- the provider-free launch preflight must run inside the admitted supervisor
  unit;
- the launch did not clear the unit name that host qualification leaves
  loaded (#270);
- resume did not clear a failed unit;
- the two ChatGPT arms received a refresh-disabled token with no lifetime
  check sized to the attempt (`CodexChatGPTCredential()` checked 0 s,
  OpenCode 390 s). An access token lasts 10 days
  ([evidence](stage-a-codex-renewal-staged-50-20260920.json)), and an expired
  one would have been recorded as the arm's authentication failure.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-06, Claude Code session)

- **Fix and re-run.** "Please fix that we need to rerun the stopped slot and
  Yeah, we'll readmit as well just try to make sure everything's fixed this
  time before we go through the whole process of re-admitting and resetting
  up everything." Attempt 3 is retired: its ledger, artifact root and
  task-input store move into its own attempt directory, and the next attempt's
  freeze runs that slot as a fresh slot.
- **One Claude confirmation per cohort.** "While we're doing this, can we make
  the Claude side use a one-year token also? I don't want to have to check in
  every day and refresh it." The Claude arm already uses the one-year setup
  token. What was daily is the owner's account-policy confirmation, then
  capped at 24 hours. The step-12 confirmation now lasts until the approved
  cohort window ends, at most 35 days (the research admission ceiling).
  - Its statement records the owner's undertaking to stop the cohort if the
    account policy changes.
  - Nothing re-checks that policy during the window.
  - Every Claude turn still checks the delivered token against the receipt.

## What changed

- **Provider credential lease.** Step 2's single masked unlock exports the
  Brave key and the four provider attachments (Claude setup token, Z.AI key,
  Meta key, Codex ChatGPT login) to private files on `/dev/shm`. A manifest
  binds each file to the admitted vault's digest. The live worker reads only
  this lease, and a missing or changed lease stops the run.
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before each reservation the launcher
  runs the next slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact boundary,
  with nothing reserved:
  - credential delivery and a ChatGPT access lifetime of at least 4,020 s;
  - Claude's token against the covering receipt;
  - the research service start and stop;
  - the sandbox and observer definition.

  It then tears all of this down before the Inspect evaluation would start. A
  failure stops the cohort with the slot pending, and a resume runs it.
- **Runbook.**
  - Step 0 refreshes the ChatGPT login before admission.
  - The launch preflight runs in the admitted unit with `systemd-run --wait`.
  - The launch inspects and clears a finished unit of the same name first.
  - A resume clears a failed unit.
  - A stopped attempt is retired before a new one, and both leases are
    removed at the end.
- **Runbook test.** The stand-in `systemd-run` gives its command `/dev/null`
  as stdin, and the shim makes any prompt inside a unit fail. The fixture
  worker and rehearsal deliver credentials from the exported lease.
- **On-host rehearsal.** `scripts/rehearse_stage_a_unattended.py` rehearses
  every arm inside a real `systemd-run` unit under the cohort's limits and
  `env -i` environment, from the candidate checkout and before re-admission,
  using an existing freeze and a copy of the research state.

## On-host rehearsal

Run on 2026-10-06 on `cachyos-asrock`, from a clean clone of this branch at
`930d72b` with `uv sync --locked`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and the staged
checkout's pinned Muse Codex build (`vendor/codex-muse/runtime`, which git does
not track) copied in. The owner exported both leases with
`rehearse_stage_a_unattended.py export` in one masked unlock, pinned to the
admitted vault digest `sha256:4450416b…c2df` (`provider_attachments=4`).

The `run` subcommand ran in the transient unit
`stage-a-unattended-rehearsal-271`:

- **Limits and environment.** `CPUQuota=100%`, `MemoryMax=2147483648`,
  `TasksMax=128`, `RuntimeMaxSec=105780`, `Nice=10`, with `env -i`
  `PATH=<runtime path>` `LANG` `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and no terminal.
- **Inputs.** Attempt 3's freeze and configuration, the retained
  `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367` image, and a copy of the research state.

Results:

- **First run.** Six arms passed. `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` failed
  with `Muse Codex runtime inventory changed` because the clone lacked the
  untracked Muse build.
- **Second run.** The rerun first needed `systemctl --user reset-failed`,
  which the runbook's resume step now documents. Receipt `rehearsal.json`
  `sha256:d3a66b1779218a3abdc27019bdb0e4bbf86823540ec0228bddd7aaeaac15ae7a`:
  - `status=passed`, with host bwrap passed;
  - every arm (`codex-gpt-5.6-sol`, `codex-glm-5.3`,
    `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, `opencode-gpt-5.6-sol`,
    `opencode-glm-5.3`, `opencode-muse-spark-1.3-contributor`,
    `claude-code-claude-opus-5`) reached the provider-contact boundary and
    confirmed cleanup;
  - the cgroup was confirmed at the supervisor limits, and the unit's memory
    peak was 1,029,058,560 bytes (of 2 GiB);
  - service runtime 67 s, `provider_requests=0`.

  This exercised, for every arm:
  - delivery from the provider lease;
  - the ChatGPT access lifetime check (the vault's token outlives a
    4,020 s attempt);
  - the Claude token against its receipt;
  - the research worker scope started from inside the unit;
  - the sandbox and observer definition on the evaluation daemon.

  Afterwards no trial container, network, research or rehearsal unit, or
  scratch directory remained, and the conserved research ledger was
  unchanged.

After the two-axis review, the code changed:

- each slot rehearsal runs its research service on a copy of the research
  state;
- a ChatGPT token must outlive the live check by the 480 s rehearsal margin;
- the step-3 receipt keeps its 24-hour cap;
- the lease is hardened, and its module is renamed `stage_a_provider_credentials`.

The rehearsal was rerun at `cb8b978`, the last code commit, with the same
leases and inputs. Receipt
`sha256:330c1729173dcef845d6f0a96574b1d58e3d16e4832dade4e077e3ae008769c9`:

- `status=passed`, with all seven arms and host bwrap passed;
- memory peak 1,028,513,792 bytes, service runtime 61 s.

Afterwards there were no containers or research units, and the conserved
`research.sqlite` was unmodified since 2026-10-06T08:00:27-04:00.

## Retirement of attempt 3

Retired on 2026-10-06, after the rehearsal and before re-admission, by the
owner's decision above.

- **First try.** The block from #271 stopped at its image release (`an
  attempt still holds the task image`), because the store refuses changes while
  the ledger at the admitted path holds an in-flight slot. Nothing had moved;
  only an empty `retired` directory existed.
- **Second try (#273).** Run in the corrected order: the ledger moved first,
  then the release (`status=released`, `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367`), then the artifact
  root. Results:
  - `state/stage-a/cohort-stage-a-reviewed-23-v1-attempt-3/retired/` holds
    `scheduler.json`, still
    `sha256:7b4f4a967d8a3f03329806d9a9a8fd5e870e20127039241f7dfa435a2d77cc41`,
    the hash at the stop, and `live/`;
  - an empty artifact root is in place.

## ChatGPT refresh before re-admission (#275)

The owner refreshed the Codex ChatGPT login in asrock's vault on 2026-10-06
at about 16:30 EDT, with the broker runbook's procedure and the pinned Codex
0.144.0. The vault moved from the owner-steps chain head
`4450416b3550c4b8d4f0fee331eda81efda6495de2b2c0a31e2d41bc2d5ec2df`, the Brave
enrollment's result and the admitted pin, to
`c3114764badccccee91fa8c6ba1534140f4e6bdfc27ed7abb8828635be62eb0b`.

The previous login dated from 2026-10-04T19:00Z, so its token would have
expired around 2026-10-14. The new one lasts until about 2026-10-16.

The owner-steps chain could not record a change after its last enrollment, and
plan building requires the Brave chain to reach the admitted vault. #275 adds
the same-account rotation record, and the refresh is recorded with it before
re-admission.

The archive's annotated tag `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` points to commit
`3c6208f49209b01786beaa3bc203f7dc8620105d` in `anodyine/multilang-task-archive`.
Its release manifest is `releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json`, SHA-256
`5dd2604bf7ef84e03ea626364c94309e3bdb3bd7250c230420ac2a0ca4febc81`. The archive
root manifest is SHA-256
`a4a1489d8e748daa723b1f874d0c6d3d1355d3da79cdfc6c5029cdf00a214bf8`.

The release selects the same 23 tasks as
[`stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`](stage-a-reviewed-23-v1.md), with the same reviewed
validators, in the same v3 selection order. What changed is that every task now
has a **prepared environment** (archive ADR 0011): a second owned image derived
from the image its validator grades in, holding the task's dependencies with an
offline configuration. Agents and image qualification run in it; graders keep
their own image
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
Stage A adopts this release in place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`; the
derived schedule is unchanged: 23 tasks × 7 standard arms = 161 slots. The
machine-readable [adoption record](stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json), SHA-256
`5f6bd0301d1833b3151e4441b47057f8313cbd6524ceac29b20c3875bacb5938`, holds the
complete corpus task entry for each task, the two exclusions and a summary. It
records `dispatch_authorized: false`.

## What differs from stage-a-reviewed-23-v1

For each task, only these binding fields differ: `archive_commit`,
`archive_manifest_sha256`, `task_metadata_sha256` and `environment_digest`. The
environment digest now pins `environment.prepared`. Source, task text,
validator, patch, parser, scorer, commands, shared validator and the grader's
`image_digest` are byte-for-byte the reviewed release's. The exclusions
(`AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` and `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180`, both `unresolved`)
and the summary's counts are unchanged.

Six tasks declare dependency paths, which the Stage A sanitizer keeps after
checking each against its recorded hash; the other 17 declare none:

| Task | Declared dependency paths |
| --- | --- |
| `kepano__defuddle-243` | `node_modules` |
| `playcanvas__engine-9066` | `node_modules` |
| `notionnext-org__NotionNext-4338` | `node_modules` |
| `mnfst__manifest-1635` | `node_modules`, `packages/backend/node_modules`, `packages/frontend/node_modules` |
| `surveyjs__survey-library-11137` | `node_modules` and five `packages/*/node_modules` |
| `mui__mui-x-22062` | 32 `node_modules` folders |

Each declared path sits in a directory the source snapshot tracks, as the
Stage A sanitizer requires. The archive's `docs/prepared-environments.md`
inventories each task's dependency steps, caches and toolchains, and its
offline qualification: every build exited 0 within 600 seconds as UID 1000
with no network, the slowest being ducklake's documented build at 353 s on 16
cores. Tests were recorded, not limited.

## Identities and compatibility

- **Cross-repository identity.** The harness binds the tag, release ID,
  release-manifest SHA-256 and archive commit (`archive_release`), and each
  task's complete `task-archive-binding/1`. The tag is never moved.
- **Schema compatibility.** The release uses `task-archive-release/1` and the
  adoption record `task-archive-adoption/1`, as before. `task_archive.inspect_release(...,
  production=True)` admits all 23 bindings.
- **Environment retention.** Every image, grader's and prepared, is an owned OCI
  layout in the owner store, restored offline with no registry pull. An
  execution host's store must hold the prepared images too: bootstrap's
  `oci-store` step syncs and checks every artifact the release's metadata names.
- **Rollback.** The adoption is additive in the archive; reverting the harness
  change returns Stage A to `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, whose record is kept.
- **Historical audit compatibility.** `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, its size record
  and every earlier freeze keep their identities and audits.

## Operator verification

On a host with the private archive repository, clone the release and confirm
its identity:

```sh

git -C /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23 checkout --detach stage-a-prepared-23-v1
git -C /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23 rev-parse HEAD
sha256sum /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json
```

Expected: the commit above, and the release-manifest SHA-256 above. Then, on the
execution host (the adoption record embeds the storage policy its registry entry
derives), from a clean checkout of this repository with the owner OCI store at
the `file://` locations the task metadata records, rebuild the adoption record:

```sh
uv tool run --from uv==0.12.9 uv run --locked python -B -m scripts.build_archive_adoption --archive /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23 --tag stage-a-prepared-23-v1 --release-id stage-a-prepared-23-v1 --corpus benchmark_corpora/swe-bench-live-multilang-stage-a-v3.json --repository ssh://tea.kyle-merritt.com:2222/anodyine/multilang-task-archive.git --output /tmp/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json
cmp /tmp/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json docs/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json
```

Expected: `"status": "verified"`, `task_count` 23, `scheduled_slots` 161, and
`cmp` prints nothing. The record was built on a workstation with Alexander's
(`alexander-evals`) registry entry standing in for the current host; the same
procedure reproduced `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1.json` byte for byte. The release
grants no dispatch, numerical freeze or provider request.

## Image sizes

[`stage-a-prepared-23-v1-image-sizes.json`](stage-a-prepared-23-v1-image-sizes.json)
(`task-archive-image-sizes/2`), SHA-256
`883ada9bb23338f429b7bc9a542cf3db5312020445483ffe0195132690b9292b`, records
each task's grader image, as the reviewed release's record does, and its
prepared `agent_image` beside it: manifest and config digests, compressed bytes
(manifest, config and layers) and the verified expanded layer bytes a
classic-store load imports. It binds the adoption record by SHA-256. The
grader images are the reviewed release's; together they expand to 139.4 GiB,
and the prepared images to 148.2 GiB. The prepared layers add from 2.5 KiB
(libarchive) to about 2 GiB (mui-x, surveyjs).

A task's preparation loads the grader's image, then the agent's while the
grader's stays loaded, and converts one at a time
(`stage_a_storage.task_preparation_bytes`). The largest is
`pola-rs__polars-28484`: about 275.7 GiB free on the Docker store and 213.2 GiB
on a separate staging filesystem, up from about 211 GiB for both. Doctor's
`storage-space` check sizes the host from this record, and the launcher
configuration's `images[task]` carries `expanded_upper_bytes` and
`agent_expanded_upper_bytes`, each `stage_a_storage.expanded_upper_estimate`
of the recorded layer bytes, which `validate_plan` requires. The record was
measured offline from the owner OCI store, with every blob and expanded layer
checked against its digest. To reproduce it on a host with that store and the
release checkout above (it reads about 290 GiB of expanded layers and writes
nothing else):

```sh
uv tool run --from uv==0.12.9 uv run --locked python -B -m scripts.measure_release_image_sizes --adoption docs/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json --oci-store ~/.local/share/multilang-task-archive/oci-store --archive /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23 --output /tmp/stage-a-prepared-23-v1-image-sizes.json
cmp /tmp/stage-a-prepared-23-v1-image-sizes.json docs/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1-image-sizes.json

The Stage A sanitizer (contract `swe-bench-repository-v2`) ran in the real
