# Cohort attempt 6

Attempt 6 ran on cachyos-asrock from 2026-10-07T21:54:59-04:00 (unit
`agent-evals-host-cf355aecf8264a36a1dc9ec7`). This record collects the
attempt's failures. Each section names the issue that fixes it.

## The run

Attempt 6 ran at commit `5d2bba5`. Its scheduler holds 161 slots, created at
2026-10-08T01:40:39Z.

- Off-host evidence: `cohort-attempt-6-launch-1-stop/evidence.tar`
  (`sha256:caba3adb70543a5e12a3ab3fb1f1d6e57cbddce2c9199421684545a6678c0aea`).
- Retired scheduler state `retired/scheduler.json`
  (`sha256:ca42f19097021f43eb2e730e65a47be8c3bfbf662f229c729f7076275b43e420`).

Twenty-eight slots ended. Fifteen recorded results (12 passed, 3 failed) and
thirteen were recorded `infrastructure_failed` / `stage_a_capability_unknown`.
The frozen retry policy makes those thirteen terminal.

| Actual order | Task | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–7 | `gfx-rs__wgpu-9367` | 7 results |
| 8–14 | `mnfst__manifest-1635` | 7 results |
| 15–20 | `xroche__httrack-893` | `infrastructure_failed`: candidate capture |
| 21 | `xroche__httrack-893` | result (`claude-code-claude-opus-5`, passed) |
| 22–28 | `github__gh-aw-27242` | `infrastructure_failed`: grade persistence |
| 29 | `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571` | interrupted, still `in_flight` |

## Lost candidates: httrack capture after an in-tree build (#282)

Fixed by #282 ([ADR 0021](../authoritative/adr/0021-exclude-untracked-build-products-from-stage-a-candidates.md),
[ADR 0023](../authoritative/adr/0023-judge-build-products-against-the-base-commit.md)): build products are
excluded from the candidate, and capture records every outcome.

### Orders 15–20

The six arms were `opencode-gpt-5.6-sol`, `opencode-muse-spark-1.3-contributor`,
`codex-glm-5.3`, `opencode-glm-5.3`, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` and
`codex-gpt-5.6-sol`. Each native run completed (`terminal.state=completed`, no
adapter failure). Each arm followed httrack's `AGENTS.md` and built in tree,
and each candidate was recorded `candidate_capture_failed`.

The capture's reason was not persisted, but each native `inspect.json` keeps
the sandbox call. Every arm failed in the submodule validator, before
`git add` or `git diff` ran:

```text
RepositorySanitizationError: edits inside submodule cannot be represented safely: src/coucal; changed paths: [".deps", ...]
```

The changed paths were all new build entries, such as `.deps/*.Plo`, `.libs/*.o`,
`*.lo`, `*.o` and `.dirstamp`, in the pinned `src/coucal` worktree. The
repository's untracked output was also left: `src/httrack`, `src/htsserver`,
`src/proxytrack`, `src/*/.dirstamp`, and `tests/*.log` with `tests/*.trs`.
The hypothesised capture output or time limit was never reached.

Claude (order 21) built out of tree in `_bld`; its candidate was captured and
passed.

## Lost grades: gh-aw grade persistence (#282)

Fixed by #282
([ADR 0022](../authoritative/adr/0022-retain-archive-grades-whose-test-names-are-secret-shaped.md)):
an archive grade persists every status with each name redacted.

### Orders 22–28

All seven arms exported a candidate, and the hidden tests ran. Each
`verification/inspect-error.json` reads:

```json
{"error_type": "UnsafeArtifactError", "message": "redaction produced duplicate artifact keys"}
```

The grade keys 26,864 statuses by test name. Two of them,
`github.com/github/gh-aw/pkg/stringutil/TestSpec_PublicAPI_ClassifyPAT/ghp__prefix_yields_classic`
and `.../gho__prefix_yields_oauth`, match the GitHub-token pattern and redacted
to the same key. The retained `grade/grade.json` and `grade/test.log` hold both
names unredacted, which the result-root secret scan would also reject.

Replayed through the fixed boundary, order 24's retained grade keeps all
26,864 statuses. The two names persist as `.../[REDACTED]` and
`.../[REDACTED]#2`, and nothing secret-shaped remains.

## Why image qualification missed both (#282)

Image qualification checked image fit, the native executables, the sanitizer
and the Claude adapter's workspace steps. It graded nothing and never built a
task:

- **httrack.** No workspace was captured in the state an agent's build leaves
  it.
- **gh-aw.** The archive's reference-patch controls are graded in the task
  archive repository, whose raw control logs are not retained. They never pass
  through this repository's persistence redaction.

Qualification now does both (ADRs 0021 and 0022).

## Stop: a lost `exec_remote` job (#283)

### Status

Fixed by #283: a lost native process is now a recorded outcome, not a stop.
That outcome is not retried. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to keep one
attempt per slot, as ADR 0016 and the v5 contract freeze it, and #288
(retries) was declined. The reasons:

- **A lost slot can't wrongly cut an arm.** It counts as
  `capability_unknown`, which sits on the arm's side of the futility rule.
- **It should be rare.** It was then read as a hang on the final poll. The
  corrected mechanism below is a replaced server, whose trigger is unconfirmed.
- **The cost is high.** Retrying would change the launcher, the Claude
  baseline, research allowance sizing, and audit and seal.

#293, which would have recovered a finished process's output, was closed: the
process had not finished. #296 makes every native sandbox failure a recorded
outcome, stops the orphaned agent before capture, and keeps the server's state
so that the next failure can name its trigger.

The Mechanism section below records retained evidence of a second way to lose
a process: the sandbox-tools server being replaced while the agent still runs.
Recovering a lost final poll does not cover that case.

### The stop

The facts in this section were observed on asrock by the owner, as reported
in #283. The pids and the kill's timing come from the retained
`native/inspect.json`.

- **When and where.** At 2026-10-08T10:56:49Z, in block 5's first slot:
  actual order 29, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` ×
  `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571`, lease
  `65c0ccf6-817e-5042-a0d0-6851a2ff7928`. Blocks 1–4 had advanced normally.
- **What failed.**
  - The launcher started Codex through Inspect's `exec_remote` at
    10:53:50.68Z. The sandbox-tools server (pid 414) returned job pid 428.
  - A poll then failed with `RuntimeError('No job found with pid 428')`. The
    failing poll is not timed (see the retry-log check).
  - The adapter's kill, sent at 10:56:47.29Z (ack_seq 43), got the same answer
    as a JSON-RPC error by 10:56:47.62Z. The sample recorded the error at
    10:56:47.89Z.
- **How the cohort stopped.** The exception escaped the Codex adapter as an
  Inspect sample error. `_run_native` then raised `native task did not
  complete`, `run_block` wrote `interrupted.json`, and the unit failed with an
  unreconciled active attempt. The cohort cannot resume.
- **Host state.** Sandbox cleanup was confirmed: no containers or networks
  remained on the eval Docker daemon. There was no OOM on the host.

### Mechanism

Read from the pinned source (inspect-ai 0.3.261, sandbox tools 1.2.1):

- **Each poll is one exec.** It is a `sandbox.exec` with a 120 s timeout and
  `timeout_retry=True`. On a timeout, the Docker sandbox silently re-runs the
  exec, up to twice.
- **The server forgets finished jobs.** `Controller.poll` retires a job as soon
  as it reports `completed` or `killed`, and `_get_job` never consults retired
  jobs.
- **So a re-run final poll fails.** If the hung exec had already delivered the
  final poll, its re-run answers `No job found`. The poll's own retry,
  `stop_after_delay(30)` measured from the first attempt, re-raises at once.

The timeline is consistent with that sequence. A poll at about 10:54:47Z hung
for 120 s, and its re-run found the job retired. The hang itself is inferred
from the timeline, not observed. #283 was fixed on that account.

**The retained evidence contradicts it.**
- **Codex had not finished.** The provider-proxy capture
  (`native/wsrf3ww0.capture/transport.jsonl`) shows 38 Codex requests from

## Stop: a lost `exec_remote` job (#283)

### Status

Fixed by #283: a lost native process is now a recorded outcome, not a stop.
That outcome is not retried. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to keep one
attempt per slot, as ADR 0016 and the v5 contract freeze it, and #288
(retries) was declined. The reasons:

- **A lost slot can't wrongly cut an arm.** It counts as
  `capability_unknown`, which sits on the arm's side of the futility rule.
- **It should be rare.** It was then read as a hang on the final poll. The
  corrected mechanism below is a replaced server, whose trigger is unconfirmed.
- **The cost is high.** Retrying would change the launcher, the Claude
  baseline, research allowance sizing, and audit and seal.

#293, which would have recovered a finished process's output, was closed: the
process had not finished. #296 makes every native sandbox failure a recorded
outcome, stops the orphaned agent before capture, and keeps the server's state
so that the next failure can name its trigger.

The Mechanism section below records retained evidence of a second way to lose
a process: the sandbox-tools server being replaced while the agent still runs.
Recovering a lost final poll does not cover that case.

### The stop

The facts in this section were observed on asrock by the owner, as reported
in #283. The pids and the kill's timing come from the retained
`native/inspect.json`.

- **When and where.** At 2026-10-08T10:56:49Z, in block 5's first slot:
  actual order 29, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` ×
  `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571`, lease
  `65c0ccf6-817e-5042-a0d0-6851a2ff7928`. Blocks 1–4 had advanced normally.
- **What failed.**
  - The launcher started Codex through Inspect's `exec_remote` at
    10:53:50.68Z. The sandbox-tools server (pid 414) returned job pid 428.
  - A poll then failed with `RuntimeError('No job found with pid 428')`. The
    failing poll is not timed (see the retry-log check).
  - The adapter's kill, sent at 10:56:47.29Z (ack_seq 43), got the same answer
    as a JSON-RPC error by 10:56:47.62Z. The sample recorded the error at
    10:56:47.89Z.
- **How the cohort stopped.** The exception escaped the Codex adapter as an
  Inspect sample error. `_run_native` then raised `native task did not
  complete`, `run_block` wrote `interrupted.json`, and the unit failed with an
  unreconciled active attempt. The cohort cannot resume.
- **Host state.** Sandbox cleanup was confirmed: no containers or networks
  remained on the eval Docker daemon. There was no OOM on the host.

### Mechanism

Read from the pinned source (inspect-ai 0.3.261, sandbox tools 1.2.1):

- **Each poll is one exec.** It is a `sandbox.exec` with a 120 s timeout and
  `timeout_retry=True`. On a timeout, the Docker sandbox silently re-runs the
  exec, up to twice.
- **The server forgets finished jobs.** `Controller.poll` retires a job as soon
  as it reports `completed` or `killed`, and `_get_job` never consults retired
  jobs.
- **So a re-run final poll fails.** If the hung exec had already delivered the
  final poll, its re-run answers `No job found`. The poll's own retry,
  `stop_after_delay(30)` measured from the first attempt, re-raises at once.

The timeline is consistent with that sequence. A poll at about 10:54:47Z hung
for 120 s, and its re-run found the job retired. The hang itself is inferred
from the timeline, not observed. #283 was fixed on that account.

**The retained evidence contradicts it.**
- **Codex had not finished.** The provider-proxy capture
  (`native/wsrf3ww0.capture/transport.jsonl`) shows 38 Codex requests from
  10:53:51Z, 1–14 seconds apart, through the supposed hang. The last one is at
  10:56:47.428Z, after the kill was sent.
- **So the job could not have been retired as finished.** A job is retired
  only after its process exits, and pid 428 was Codex itself: `/bin/sh -c`,
  `env` and `sh -c 'exec "$@"'` all `exec`.

**The server was most likely replaced while Codex ran.** Read from the same
pinned source:
- **The client restarts a server it can't reach.** Before every call, the
  sandbox-tools client checks the server's socket in `/tmp/sandbox-tools/`. If
  it cannot reach it, it starts a new server with an empty job registry.
- **The old job runs on.** Jobs are plain children of the old server, so they
  keep running as orphans.
- **This fits the stop.** The kill was answered by a live server, with a
  JSON-RPC error rather than a transport failure. Codex kept calling the
  provider until the container was removed.

**The trigger is unconfirmed.** The adapter kept none of Codex's stream. The
candidates are all within the agent's reach:
- **Killing the server.** The agent runs as the same user as the server, in one
  process namespace, with Codex's own sandbox bypassed.
- **Removing its state.** The server's socket and pid file are on the agent's
  64 MiB `/tmp` tmpfs.
- **A server crash.** The host showed no OOM.

**Settling it next time.** From #296 on, a lost process records, before
teardown, the server identified when the job started and whether it is still
alive, the current server, the state directory's listing and the tail of
`server-stderr.log`. A different current server confirms a replacement, and
the partial stream that #283 persists shows the agent's last commands.

### Prevention: agents run unprivileged

The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (#296) that every arm's agent will run as an
unprivileged user, with the sandbox-tools server out of its reach. Running all
arms at the same privilege level also keeps the comparison even. Today every
arm's agent runs as the container's root user, like the server; only Claude
Code's MCP bridge drops to another user. The change is tracked separately
(#300); until it lands, a failure is recorded and the agent stopped, but
not prevented.

### Retry-log check

The owner inspected the interrupted sample's `native/inspect.json` once asrock
was reachable again. It holds no `logger` events, only 44 `sandbox` events,
spans, `sample_init` and the error. Polls run under `no_events()`, so the
transcript can neither confirm nor rule out a `Retrying docker compose command
after TimeoutError` re-run.

From #283 on, the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll. The native stream
re-polls a timed-out poll itself, and the adapter records the count as
`diagnostics.native_process.poll_timeouts`. A future stop therefore names its
poll timeouts directly.

### Upstream

Inspect 0.3.277 (2026-10-06) adds opt-in `poll_timeout_recovery`, which
re-polls after a timeout. Its sandbox tools v33 also make kill safer after a
process has exited. Neither keeps a retired job answerable: a lost final poll
still raises, as "the process most likely ended during the stall". A pin bump
would therefore not have prevented this stop.

## Status

Implemented in the harness for #271. The provider-free on-host rehearsal
result is recorded below. Attempt 3 is retired and attempt 4 is prepared only
after this change merges and asrock is re-admitted at its commit.

## The stop

Cohort attempt 3 on `cachyos-asrock` used freeze
`sha256:735f29e099a98b88ac982c891f9516ebaa50be6617c643aa06683363ff2e889b`,
which binds the admitted host profile
`sha256:5d890be13e19e9076558d4927af4c49704ad7d84a3b81b426d375cd55b4315e9` at

  earlier. The ledger now holds one `in_flight` slot and 160 `pending`, and

## Why tests did not catch it

No test had run the live worker's credential path in a process without a
terminal:

- the execution tests replace `run_native`;
- the vault tests replace `getpass`;
- the runbook test's interpreter shim reported `isatty()` as true for every
  command, including the one its stand-in `systemd-run` started.

A read-only audit of the live path found these further defects, which would
have stopped or corrupted the cohort later:

- the provider-free launch preflight must run inside the admitted supervisor
  unit;
- the launch did not clear the unit name that host qualification leaves
  loaded (#270);
- resume did not clear a failed unit;
- the two ChatGPT arms received a refresh-disabled token with no lifetime
  check sized to the attempt (`CodexChatGPTCredential()` checked 0 s,
  OpenCode 390 s). An access token lasts 10 days
  ([evidence](stage-a-codex-renewal-staged-50-20260920.json)), and an expired
  one would have been recorded as the arm's authentication failure.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-06, Claude Code session)

- **Fix and re-run.** "Please fix that we need to rerun the stopped slot and
  Yeah, we'll readmit as well just try to make sure everything's fixed this
  time before we go through the whole process of re-admitting and resetting
  up everything." Attempt 3 is retired: its ledger, artifact root and
  task-input store move into its own attempt directory, and the next attempt's
  freeze runs that slot as a fresh slot.
- **One Claude confirmation per cohort.** "While we're doing this, can we make
  the Claude side use a one-year token also? I don't want to have to check in
  every day and refresh it." The Claude arm already uses the one-year setup
  token. What was daily is the owner's account-policy confirmation, then
  capped at 24 hours. The step-12 confirmation now lasts until the approved
  cohort window ends, at most 35 days (the research admission ceiling).
  - Its statement records the owner's undertaking to stop the cohort if the
    account policy changes.
  - Nothing re-checks that policy during the window.
  - Every Claude turn still checks the delivered token against the receipt.

## What changed

- **Provider credential lease.** Step 2's single masked unlock exports the
  Brave key and the four provider attachments (Claude setup token, Z.AI key,
  Meta key, Codex ChatGPT login) to private files on `/dev/shm`. A manifest
  binds each file to the admitted vault's digest. The live worker reads only
  this lease, and a missing or changed lease stops the run.
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before each reservation the launcher
  runs the next slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact boundary,
  with nothing reserved:
  - credential delivery and a ChatGPT access lifetime of at least 4,020 s;
  - Claude's token against the covering receipt;
  - the research service start and stop;
  - the sandbox and observer definition.

  It then tears all of this down before the Inspect evaluation would start. A
  failure stops the cohort with the slot pending, and a resume runs it.
- **Runbook.**
  - Step 0 refreshes the ChatGPT login before admission.
  - The launch preflight runs in the admitted unit with `systemd-run --wait`.
  - The launch inspects and clears a finished unit of the same name first.
  - A resume clears a failed unit.
  - A stopped attempt is retired before a new one, and both leases are
    removed at the end.
- **Runbook test.** The stand-in `systemd-run` gives its command `/dev/null`
  as stdin, and the shim makes any prompt inside a unit fail. The fixture
  worker and rehearsal deliver credentials from the exported lease.
- **On-host rehearsal.** `scripts/rehearse_stage_a_unattended.py` rehearses
  every arm inside a real `systemd-run` unit under the cohort's limits and
  `env -i` environment, from the candidate checkout and before re-admission,
  using an existing freeze and a copy of the research state.

# Run agents in prepared environments, keeping their declared dependency paths

## Context

A Stage A agent works offline, as the unprivileged agent user
([ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)), in its task
image's `/testbed` after repository sanitization. Sanitization rebuilds Git
from the base commit and runs `git clean -ffdx`, which removes every ignored
dependency folder inside the repository, such as `node_modules`. The agent
cannot read the caches and toolchains the image keeps under a mode-0700
`/root`. So in the agent's workspace most tasks could not build their own
code offline. Cohort attempt 9 (#24) showed both effects:

- surveyjs's offline `npm install` outlived its in-place build's 6,467-second
  share and stopped image qualification;
- 12 of the 18 tasks that qualified had grader builds that exited nonzero as
  the agent.

The owner decided (2026-10-11, multilang-task-archive #76) that dependencies
are prepared ahead of time and belong to each task's environment, for agents
and qualification alike. The archive's ADR 0011 records each task's
**prepared environment**. It is a second owned image derived from the image
the task's selected validator grades in. Its caches and toolchains are moved
out of `/root`, its offline configuration is in the image's `Env`, and its
dependency folders inside the repository are **declared dependency paths**.
Each declared path is recorded with the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of its
`_filesystem_entries` inventory, the same entry shape and order as this
repository's sanitizer. Graders never run in a prepared environment.

The sanitizer `swe_bench_workspace.py` (contract `swe-bench-repository-v1`) is
pinned by its SHA-256 in frozen instruments:

- the MultiLang v1 to v3 corpora and their sanitizer runner bundle;
- the control-reuse and successor reproducibility checks;
- the SWE-bench Verified task manifest.

A one-byte change to it fails 10 tests that pass on `main`, and leaves the
frozen v3 corpus unexecutable. [ADR 0021](0021-exclude-untracked-build-products-from-stage-a-candidates.md)
kept it unchanged for the same reason.

## Decision

**The agent's image is the prepared environment.** An archive task's agent
sandbox and its image qualification run in the artifact that
`environment.prepared.artifact_id` names. It is restored offline from the
owner store, like the grader's image. Graders keep the image their validator
names (the binding's `image_digest`). The binding's `environment_digest` pins
the prepared environment, and `task_archive.prepared_environment` accepts it
only if all of these hold:

- the artifact is neither the primary nor any validator's;
- its definition names the bound grader image as its base and this artifact
  as the prepared one;
- its declared paths are the definition's.

The selection carries the agent's image (`agent_image`) and the declared paths
beside the grader's image, and `validate_selection` re-derives both.

**One lifecycle holds both images.** `TaskImageStore.prepare` loads the
grader's image, then the agent's, and records both. `check` serves either, and
`release` removes the agent's image first, since it extends the grader's
layers. The grader's image stays loaded while the agent's converts and loads.
So the Docker store needs the larger of the grader's preparation and the
grader's expanded bound plus the agent image's preparation. Conversion stages
one image at a time, so the staging filesystem needs only the larger single
preparation. The release image size record `task-archive-image-sizes/2`
measures each task's agent image beside its grader's. The configuration
carries each agent image's `agent_expanded_upper_bytes`, which `validate_plan`
requires to be the record's estimate. Doctor sizes the store and staging this
way.

**Sanitizer contract v2 keeps exactly the declared paths.** The Stage A
sanitizer is `stage_a_workspace.py`, contract `swe-bench-repository-v2`. It
runs in the sandbox beside an unchanged copy of `swe_bench_workspace.py` and
imports its helpers, so no frozen pin moves. Its identity hashes both files.
It runs v1's steps, with these changes:

- **Refusals, before anything changes.** Each declared path must be
  repository-relative and canonical, with no `.`, `..` or `.git` part. It must
  not be tracked, hold tracked files, be nested in another declared path or
  overlap a runtime mount, and it must sit directly in a tracked directory or
  at the root.
- **The clean keeps them.** `git clean -ffdx` excludes each declared path, as
  it excludes the image's empty runtime mountpoints. Every other ignored or
  untracked file is still removed.
- **Each is checked against its hash.** Once the workspace is final, each
  declared path must be a real directory whose inventory hash equals its
  recorded one. A missing or changed path fails sanitization by name:
  `declared dependency path differs from its recorded hash: <path>`.
- **The boundary admits them whole.** The workspace boundary admits each
  declared path without listing its content, which the hash check covers.
- **The evidence records them.** The evidence lists the kept paths as
  `dependency_paths` and carries the v2 identity, which Stage A's workspace
  preparation requires.

The SWE-bench Verified path, the MultiLang verifier and the frozen corpora keep
v1.

**A declared path is environment, never candidate.** Nothing in it is ever
part of a patch:

- Stage A capture's staging program never stages it. It also unstages
  whatever the agent staged or committed inside it, whether or not the
  repository ignores the folder.
- The archive's host-side capture excludes it from its intent-to-add and its
  diff.
- The Claude adapter leaves it out of its baseline snapshot and its own
  candidate export. Qualification's timing of those steps leaves it out too.

**Adoption.** Stage A adopts the archive release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` in
place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, under
[ADR 0016](0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)'s binding rule. It
holds the same 23 tasks, validators and order. Its bindings differ only in the
archive commit and manifest, each task's metadata hash and its environment
digest, because each task now declares a prepared environment. Every task has
one; six declare dependency paths:

| Task | Declared paths |
| --- | --- |
| defuddle, playcanvas, NotionNext | `node_modules` |
| manifest | 3 |
| surveyjs | 6 |
| mui-x | 32 |

The release record is [stage-a-prepared-23-v1](../../releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.md).

## Consequences

- An agent starts with its task's dependencies installed and readable, as on
  a developer's machine. It can build and test offline without reinstalling.
- The agent's environment differs from the grader's only by the prepared
  dependencies and configuration. Grades, validators and review evidence stand.
- Sanitizing a prepared workspace hashes every declared file once. In the real
  prepared images, offline, it took 5.3 s for manifest's 3 paths, 17.9 s for
  surveyjs's 6 and 32.9 s for mui-x's 32, well inside the setup phase. Exactly
  the declared paths remained in each.
- Preparing a task loads two images. Doctor's store requirement for the
  largest task grows by about that task's expanded image. The staging
  requirement grows only by the agent image's own preparation.
- An agent's change inside a declared path, such as a patched dependency, is
  never graded.
- Every arm runs in a new environment and sandbox implementation. The
  execution host, every arm's admission, image qualification and the freeze
  are redone at the new commit, as [ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md#re-admission-and-freeze)
  describes for a sandbox change.
- Known limits carried, not fixed:
  - **surveyjs.** Its grader's test command names root's Chrome path, which
    the agent cannot reach. The prepared image's `CHROME_BIN` names the moved
    browser.
  - **wgpu.** Its tests need the untracked `.gpuconfig` that sanitization
    removes. An agent can regenerate it with `cargo xtask test`.

# Prepared 23-task Stage A archive input

The archive's annotated tag `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` points to commit
`3c6208f49209b01786beaa3bc203f7dc8620105d` in `anodyine/multilang-task-archive`.
Its release manifest is `releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json`, SHA-256
`5dd2604bf7ef84e03ea626364c94309e3bdb3bd7250c230420ac2a0ca4febc81`. The archive
root manifest is SHA-256
`a4a1489d8e748daa723b1f874d0c6d3d1355d3da79cdfc6c5029cdf00a214bf8`.

The release selects the same 23 tasks as
[`stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`](stage-a-reviewed-23-v1.md), with the same reviewed
validators, in the same v3 selection order. What changed is that every task now
has a **prepared environment** (archive ADR 0011): a second owned image derived
from the image its validator grades in, holding the task's dependencies with an
offline configuration. Agents and image qualification run in it; graders keep
their own image
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
Stage A adopts this release in place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`; the
derived schedule is unchanged: 23 tasks × 7 standard arms = 161 slots. The
machine-readable [adoption record](stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json), SHA-256
`5f6bd0301d1833b3151e4441b47057f8313cbd6524ceac29b20c3875bacb5938`, holds the
complete corpus task entry for each task, the two exclusions and a summary. It
records `dispatch_authorized: false`.

## What differs from stage-a-reviewed-23-v1

For each task, only these binding fields differ: `archive_commit`,
`archive_manifest_sha256`, `task_metadata_sha256` and `environment_digest`. The
environment digest now pins `environment.prepared`. Source, task text,
validator, patch, parser, scorer, commands, shared validator and the grader's
`image_digest` are byte-for-byte the reviewed release's. The exclusions
(`AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` and `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180`, both `unresolved`)
and the summary's counts are unchanged.

Six tasks declare dependency paths, which the Stage A sanitizer keeps after
checking each against its recorded hash; the other 17 declare none:

| Task | Declared dependency paths |
| --- | --- |
| `kepano__defuddle-243` | `node_modules` |
| `playcanvas__engine-9066` | `node_modules` |
| `notionnext-org__NotionNext-4338` | `node_modules` |
| `mnfst__manifest-1635` | `node_modules`, `packages/backend/node_modules`, `packages/frontend/node_modules` |
| `surveyjs__survey-library-11137` | `node_modules` and five `packages/*/node_modules` |
| `mui__mui-x-22062` | 32 `node_modules` folders |

Each declared path sits in a directory the source snapshot tracks, as the
Stage A sanitizer requires. The archive's `docs/prepared-environments.md`
inventories each task's dependency steps, caches and toolchains, and its
offline qualification: every build exited 0 within 600 seconds as UID 1000
with no network, the slowest being ducklake's documented build at 353 s on 16
cores. Tests were recorded, not limited.

## Identities and compatibility

- **Cross-repository identity.** The harness binds the tag, release ID,
  release-manifest SHA-256 and archive commit (`archive_release`), and each
  task's complete `task-archive-binding/1`. The tag is never moved.
- **Schema compatibility.** The release uses `task-archive-release/1` and the
  adoption record `task-archive-adoption/1`, as before. `task_archive.inspect_release(...,
  production=True)` admits all 23 bindings.
- **Environment retention.** Every image, grader's and prepared, is an owned OCI
  layout in the owner store, restored offline with no registry pull. An
  execution host's store must hold the prepared images too: bootstrap's
  `oci-store` step syncs and checks every artifact the release's metadata names.
- **Rollback.** The adoption is additive in the archive; reverting the harness
  change returns Stage A to `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, whose record is kept.
- **Historical audit compatibility.** `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, its size record
  and every earlier freeze keep their identities and audits.

## Operator verification

On a host with the private archive repository, clone the release and confirm
its identity:

```sh
git clone ssh://git@tea.kyle-merritt.com:2222/anodyine/multilang-task-archive.git /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23
git -C /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23 checkout --detach stage-a-prepared-23-v1
git -C /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23 rev-parse HEAD
sha256sum /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json
```

## Stop: a lost `exec_remote` job (#283)

### Status

Fixed by #283: a lost native process is now a recorded outcome, not a stop.
That outcome is not retried. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to keep one
attempt per slot, as ADR 0016 and the v5 contract freeze it, and #288
(retries) was declined. The reasons:

- **A lost slot can't wrongly cut an arm.** It counts as
  `capability_unknown`, which sits on the arm's side of the futility rule.
- **It should be rare.** It was then read as a hang on the final poll. The
  corrected mechanism below is a replaced server, whose trigger is unconfirmed.
- **The cost is high.** Retrying would change the launcher, the Claude
  baseline, research allowance sizing, and audit and seal.

#293, which would have recovered a finished process's output, was closed: the
process had not finished. #296 makes every native sandbox failure a recorded
outcome, stops the orphaned agent before capture, and keeps the server's state
so that the next failure can name its trigger.

The Mechanism section below records retained evidence of a second way to lose
a process: the sandbox-tools server being replaced while the agent still runs.
Recovering a lost final poll does not cover that case.

### The stop

The facts in this section were observed on asrock by the owner, as reported
in #283. The pids and the kill's timing come from the retained
`native/inspect.json`.

- **When and where.** At 2026-10-08T10:56:49Z, in block 5's first slot:
  actual order 29, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` ×
  `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571`, lease
  `65c0ccf6-817e-5042-a0d0-6851a2ff7928`. Blocks 1–4 had advanced normally.
- **What failed.**
  - The launcher started Codex through Inspect's `exec_remote` at
    10:53:50.68Z. The sandbox-tools server (pid 414) returned job pid 428.
  - A poll then failed with `RuntimeError('No job found with pid 428')`. The
    failing poll is not timed (see the retry-log check).
  - The adapter's kill, sent at 10:56:47.29Z (ack_seq 43), got the same answer
    as a JSON-RPC error by 10:56:47.62Z. The sample recorded the error at
    10:56:47.89Z.
- **How the cohort stopped.** The exception escaped the Codex adapter as an
  Inspect sample error. `_run_native` then raised `native task did not
  complete`, `run_block` wrote `interrupted.json`, and the unit failed with an
  unreconciled active attempt. The cohort cannot resume.
- **Host state.** Sandbox cleanup was confirmed: no containers or networks
  remained on the eval Docker daemon. There was no OOM on the host.

### Mechanism

Read from the pinned source (inspect-ai 0.3.261, sandbox tools 1.2.1):

- **Each poll is one exec.** It is a `sandbox.exec` with a 120 s timeout and
  `timeout_retry=True`. On a timeout, the Docker sandbox silently re-runs the
  exec, up to twice.
- **The server forgets finished jobs.** `Controller.poll` retires a job as soon
  as it reports `completed` or `killed`, and `_get_job` never consults retired
  jobs.
- **So a re-run final poll fails.** If the hung exec had already delivered the
  final poll, its re-run answers `No job found`. The poll's own retry,
  `stop_after_delay(30)` measured from the first attempt, re-raises at once.

The timeline is consistent with that sequence. A poll at about 10:54:47Z hung
for 120 s, and its re-run found the job retired. The hang itself is inferred
from the timeline, not observed. #283 was fixed on that account.

**The retained evidence contradicts it.**
- **Codex had not finished.** The provider-proxy capture
  (`native/wsrf3ww0.capture/transport.jsonl`) shows 38 Codex requests from
  10:53:51Z, 1–14 seconds apart, through the supposed hang. The last one is at
  10:56:47.428Z, after the kill was sent.
- **So the job could not have been retired as finished.** A job is retired
  only after its process exits, and pid 428 was Codex itself: `/bin/sh -c`,
  `env` and `sh -c 'exec "$@"'` all `exec`.

**The server was most likely replaced while Codex ran.** Read from the same
pinned source:
- **The client restarts a server it can't reach.** Before every call, the
  sandbox-tools client checks the server's socket in `/tmp/sandbox-tools/`. If
  it cannot reach it, it starts a new server with an empty job registry.
- **The old job runs on.** Jobs are plain children of the old server, so they
  keep running as orphans.
- **This fits the stop.** The kill was answered by a live server, with a
  JSON-RPC error rather than a transport failure. Codex kept calling the
  provider until the container was removed.

**The trigger is unconfirmed.** The adapter kept none of Codex's stream. The
candidates are all within the agent's reach:
- **Killing the server.** The agent runs as the same user as the server, in one
  process namespace, with Codex's own sandbox bypassed.
- **Removing its state.** The server's socket and pid file are on the agent's
  64 MiB `/tmp` tmpfs.
- **A server crash.** The host showed no OOM.

**Settling it next time.** From #296 on, a lost process records, before
teardown, the server identified when the job started and whether it is still
alive, the current server, the state directory's listing and the tail of
`server-stderr.log`. A different current server confirms a replacement, and
the partial stream that #283 persists shows the agent's last commands.

### Prevention: agents run unprivileged

The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (#296) that every arm's agent will run as an
unprivileged user, with the sandbox-tools server out of its reach. Running all
arms at the same privilege level also keeps the comparison even. Today every
arm's agent runs as the container's root user, like the server; only Claude
Code's MCP bridge drops to another user. The change is tracked separately
(#300); until it lands, a failure is recorded and the agent stopped, but
not prevented.

### Retry-log check

The owner inspected the interrupted sample's `native/inspect.json` once asrock
was reachable again. It holds no `logger` events, only 44 `sandbox` events,
spans, `sample_init` and the error. Polls run under `no_events()`, so the
transcript can neither confirm nor rule out a `Retrying docker compose command
after TimeoutError` re-run.

From #283 on, the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll. The native stream
re-polls a timed-out poll itself, and the adapter records the count as
`diagnostics.native_process.poll_timeouts`. A future stop therefore names its
poll timeouts directly.

### Upstream

Inspect 0.3.277 (2026-10-06) adds opt-in `poll_timeout_recovery`, which
re-polls after a timeout. Its sandbox tools v33 also make kill safer after a
process has exited. Neither keeps a retired job answerable: a lost final poll
still raises, as "the process most likely ended during the stall". A pin bump
would therefore not have prevented this stop.

# Run agents in prepared environments, keeping their declared dependency paths

## Context

A Stage A agent works offline, as the unprivileged agent user
([ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)), in its task
image's `/testbed` after repository sanitization. Sanitization rebuilds Git
from the base commit and runs `git clean -ffdx`, which removes every ignored
dependency folder inside the repository, such as `node_modules`. The agent
cannot read the caches and toolchains the image keeps under a mode-0700
`/root`. So in the agent's workspace most tasks could not build their own
code offline. Cohort attempt 9 (#24) showed both effects:

- surveyjs's offline `npm install` outlived its in-place build's 6,467-second
  share and stopped image qualification;
- 12 of the 18 tasks that qualified had grader builds that exited nonzero as
  the agent.

The owner decided (2026-10-11, multilang-task-archive #76) that dependencies
are prepared ahead of time and belong to each task's environment, for agents
and qualification alike. The archive's ADR 0011 records each task's
**prepared environment**. It is a second owned image derived from the image
the task's selected validator grades in. Its caches and toolchains are moved
out of `/root`, its offline configuration is in the image's `Env`, and its
dependency folders inside the repository are **declared dependency paths**.
Each declared path is recorded with the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of its
`_filesystem_entries` inventory, the same entry shape and order as this
repository's sanitizer. Graders never run in a prepared environment.

The sanitizer `swe_bench_workspace.py` (contract `swe-bench-repository-v1`) is
pinned by its SHA-256 in frozen instruments:

- the MultiLang v1 to v3 corpora and their sanitizer runner bundle;
- the control-reuse and successor reproducibility checks;
- the SWE-bench Verified task manifest.

A one-byte change to it fails 10 tests that pass on `main`, and leaves the
frozen v3 corpus unexecutable. [ADR 0021](0021-exclude-untracked-build-products-from-stage-a-candidates.md)
kept it unchanged for the same reason.

## Decision

**The agent's image is the prepared environment.** An archive task's agent
sandbox and its image qualification run in the artifact that
`environment.prepared.artifact_id` names. It is restored offline from the
owner store, like the grader's image. Graders keep the image their validator
names (the binding's `image_digest`). The binding's `environment_digest` pins
the prepared environment, and `task_archive.prepared_environment` accepts it
only if all of these hold:

- the artifact is neither the primary nor any validator's;
- its definition names the bound grader image as its base and this artifact
  as the prepared one;
- its declared paths are the definition's.

The selection carries the agent's image (`agent_image`) and the declared paths
beside the grader's image, and `validate_selection` re-derives both.

**One lifecycle holds both images.** `TaskImageStore.prepare` loads the
grader's image, then the agent's, and records both. `check` serves either, and
`release` removes the agent's image first, since it extends the grader's
layers. The grader's image stays loaded while the agent's converts and loads.
So the Docker store needs the larger of the grader's preparation and the
grader's expanded bound plus the agent image's preparation. Conversion stages
one image at a time, so the staging filesystem needs only the larger single
preparation. The release image size record `task-archive-image-sizes/2`
measures each task's agent image beside its grader's. The configuration
carries each agent image's `agent_expanded_upper_bytes`, which `validate_plan`
requires to be the record's estimate. Doctor sizes the store and staging this
way.

**Sanitizer contract v2 keeps exactly the declared paths.** The Stage A
sanitizer is `stage_a_workspace.py`, contract `swe-bench-repository-v2`. It
runs in the sandbox beside an unchanged copy of `swe_bench_workspace.py` and
imports its helpers, so no frozen pin moves. Its identity hashes both files.
It runs v1's steps, with these changes:

- **Refusals, before anything changes.** Each declared path must be
  repository-relative and canonical, with no `.`, `..` or `.git` part. It must
  not be tracked, hold tracked files, be nested in another declared path or
  overlap a runtime mount, and it must sit directly in a tracked directory or
  at the root.
- **The clean keeps them.** `git clean -ffdx` excludes each declared path, as
  it excludes the image's empty runtime mountpoints. Every other ignored or
  untracked file is still removed.
- **Each is checked against its hash.** Once the workspace is final, each
  declared path must be a real directory whose inventory hash equals its
  recorded one. A missing or changed path fails sanitization by name:
  `declared dependency path differs from its recorded hash: <path>`.
- **The boundary admits them whole.** The workspace boundary admits each
  declared path without listing its content, which the hash check covers.
- **The evidence records them.** The evidence lists the kept paths as
  `dependency_paths` and carries the v2 identity, which Stage A's workspace
  preparation requires.

The SWE-bench Verified path, the MultiLang verifier and the frozen corpora keep
v1.

**A declared path is environment, never candidate.** Nothing in it is ever
part of a patch:

- Stage A capture's staging program never stages it. It also unstages
  whatever the agent staged or committed inside it, whether or not the
  repository ignores the folder.
- The archive's host-side capture excludes it from its intent-to-add and its
  diff.
- The Claude adapter leaves it out of its baseline snapshot and its own
  candidate export. Qualification's timing of those steps leaves it out too.

**Adoption.** Stage A adopts the archive release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` in
place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, under
[ADR 0016](0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)'s binding rule. It
holds the same 23 tasks, validators and order. Its bindings differ only in the
archive commit and manifest, each task's metadata hash and its environment
digest, because each task now declares a prepared environment. Every task has
one; six declare dependency paths:

| Task | Declared paths |
| --- | --- |
| defuddle, playcanvas, NotionNext | `node_modules` |
| manifest | 3 |
| surveyjs | 6 |
| mui-x | 32 |

The release record is [stage-a-prepared-23-v1](../../releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.md).

## Consequences

- An agent starts with its task's dependencies installed and readable, as on
  a developer's machine. It can build and test offline without reinstalling.
- The agent's environment differs from the grader's only by the prepared
  dependencies and configuration. Grades, validators and review evidence stand.
- Sanitizing a prepared workspace hashes every declared file once. In the real
  prepared images, offline, it took 5.3 s for manifest's 3 paths, 17.9 s for
  surveyjs's 6 and 32.9 s for mui-x's 32, well inside the setup phase. Exactly
  the declared paths remained in each.
- Preparing a task loads two images. Doctor's store requirement for the
  largest task grows by about that task's expanded image. The staging
  requirement grows only by the agent image's own preparation.
- An agent's change inside a declared path, such as a patched dependency, is
  never graded.
- Every arm runs in a new environment and sandbox implementation. The
  execution host, every arm's admission, image qualification and the freeze
  are redone at the new commit, as [ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md#re-admission-and-freeze)
  describes for a sandbox change.
- Known limits carried, not fixed:
  - **surveyjs.** Its grader's test command names root's Chrome path, which
    the agent cannot reach. The prepared image's `CHROME_BIN` names the moved
    browser.
  - **wgpu.** Its tests need the untracked `.gpuconfig` that sanitization
    removes. An agent can regenerate it with `cargo xtask test`.

# Prepared 23-task Stage A archive input

The archive's annotated tag `stage-a-prepared-23-v1` points to commit
`3c6208f49209b01786beaa3bc203f7dc8620105d` in `anodyine/multilang-task-archive`.
Its release manifest is `releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json`, SHA-256
`5dd2604bf7ef84e03ea626364c94309e3bdb3bd7250c230420ac2a0ca4febc81`. The archive
root manifest is SHA-256
`a4a1489d8e748daa723b1f874d0c6d3d1355d3da79cdfc6c5029cdf00a214bf8`.

The release selects the same 23 tasks as
[`stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`](stage-a-reviewed-23-v1.md), with the same reviewed
validators, in the same v3 selection order. What changed is that every task now
has a **prepared environment** (archive ADR 0011): a second owned image derived
from the image its validator grades in, holding the task's dependencies with an
offline configuration. Agents and image qualification run in it; graders keep
their own image
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
Stage A adopts this release in place of `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`; the
derived schedule is unchanged: 23 tasks × 7 standard arms = 161 slots. The
machine-readable [adoption record](stage-a-prepared-23-v1.json), SHA-256
`5f6bd0301d1833b3151e4441b47057f8313cbd6524ceac29b20c3875bacb5938`, holds the
complete corpus task entry for each task, the two exclusions and a summary. It
records `dispatch_authorized: false`.

## What differs from stage-a-reviewed-23-v1

For each task, only these binding fields differ: `archive_commit`,
`archive_manifest_sha256`, `task_metadata_sha256` and `environment_digest`. The
environment digest now pins `environment.prepared`. Source, task text,
validator, patch, parser, scorer, commands, shared validator and the grader's
`image_digest` are byte-for-byte the reviewed release's. The exclusions
(`AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` and `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180`, both `unresolved`)
and the summary's counts are unchanged.

Six tasks declare dependency paths, which the Stage A sanitizer keeps after
checking each against its recorded hash; the other 17 declare none:

| Task | Declared dependency paths |
| --- | --- |
| `kepano__defuddle-243` | `node_modules` |
| `playcanvas__engine-9066` | `node_modules` |
| `notionnext-org__NotionNext-4338` | `node_modules` |
| `mnfst__manifest-1635` | `node_modules`, `packages/backend/node_modules`, `packages/frontend/node_modules` |
| `surveyjs__survey-library-11137` | `node_modules` and five `packages/*/node_modules` |
| `mui__mui-x-22062` | 32 `node_modules` folders |

Each declared path sits in a directory the source snapshot tracks, as the
Stage A sanitizer requires. The archive's `docs/prepared-environments.md`
inventories each task's dependency steps, caches and toolchains, and its
offline qualification: every build exited 0 within 600 seconds as UID 1000
with no network, the slowest being ducklake's documented build at 353 s on 16
cores. Tests were recorded, not limited.

## Identities and compatibility

- **Cross-repository identity.** The harness binds the tag, release ID,
  release-manifest SHA-256 and archive commit (`archive_release`), and each
  task's complete `task-archive-binding/1`. The tag is never moved.
- **Schema compatibility.** The release uses `task-archive-release/1` and the
  adoption record `task-archive-adoption/1`, as before. `task_archive.inspect_release(...,
  production=True)` admits all 23 bindings.
- **Environment retention.** Every image, grader's and prepared, is an owned OCI
  layout in the owner store, restored offline with no registry pull. An
  execution host's store must hold the prepared images too: bootstrap's
  `oci-store` step syncs and checks every artifact the release's metadata names.
- **Rollback.** The adoption is additive in the archive; reverting the harness
  change returns Stage A to `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, whose record is kept.
- **Historical audit compatibility.** `stage-a-reviewed-23-v1`, its size record
  and every earlier freeze keep their identities and audits.

## Operator verification

On a host with the private archive repository, clone the release and confirm
its identity:

```sh
git clone ssh://git@tea.kyle-merritt.com:2222/anodyine/multilang-task-archive.git /tmp/multilang-stage-a-prepared-23

(`task-archive-image-sizes/2`), SHA-256
`883ada9bb23338f429b7bc9a542cf3db5312020445483ffe0195132690b9292b`, records
each task's grader image, as the reviewed release's record does, and its

**Evaluating publication status**

I’m considering the potential status of “not yet published” versus a claim of completeness. It seems like I need to reference historical attempts in this context. I want to strike a balance—making the information concise yet detailed enough to be meaningful. There’s a lot around publication statuses that can be confusing, and I want to present it clearly so that it’s easy to understand for whoever is reading it.

**No.** The 35 outcomes are a completed *operational qualification*, not the comparative Stage A cohort. The README says both that the live gate recorded 31 passes, three verifier failures and one timeout, and that a complete comparative Stage A has **not** been published ([`README.md`](agent-harness-evals/README.md), “Current execution”).

The final qualification record establishes that all **35 seven-arm × five-task slots** were recorded and audited, with zero unresolved slots. It also records **36 attempts** because an original OpenCode/Sol infrastructure failure was retained before an authorized successor attempt. The three Matplotlib failures were valid unsuccessful patches; the GLM deadline was an eligible terminal score of zero, not missing data. Results span **four documented execution revisions** and five Python SWE-bench projects. Thus they support the live execution, capture, verification, recovery and accounting gate—not a uniform-revision capability comparison or a MultiLang ranking ([`docs/evidence/current-qualification-180-final.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/evidence/current-qualification-180-final.md), “Complete task matrix,” “Investigation dispositions,” and “Final implementation validation”; [`docs/runbooks/current-qualification.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/runbooks/current-qualification.md), “Verification and limits”).

**The current Stage A contract is a different experiment.** The selected 25-task MultiLang corpus remains a pinned historical input, but the amended executable screen uses **23 reviewed archive tasks**, seven standard arms, one repetition and **161 scheduled slots**. Two validator-unresolved tasks were dropped without replacement; the prepared-environment release retains the 23 tasks, validators and order. The README’s opening “25-task” shorthand—and older 25-task/175-slot planning passages—should not be read as overriding that amendment ([`docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md), “Stage A — screening cohort”; [`docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md); [`docs/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/releases/stage-a-prepared-23-v1.md)).

A comparative run requires its **own** exact, owner-approved numerical freeze: archive/corpus and verifier identities, all seven freshly admitted arm/runtime/research identities, policy, finite window, resources and reservations, seeded complete schedule and outcome-slot plan. The continuous cohort must use one ledger and admitted configuration, reconcile every slot, then receive a full offline audit, Stage A seal and separate published report/disposition. Earlier Glaze blocks and stopped cohort attempts are not a prefix to substitute for that cohort ([`docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md), “Executable freeze boundary,” “Stage A,” and “Screening report”; [`docs/runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md), “What the harness enforces”; [`docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).

**Still unverified by the qualification:** a sealed, published 161-slot comparative screen; a precise ordering of seven arms; run-to-run reliability from a one-repetition screen; or a Stage B/RelayView comparison. Stage A’s prospective futility test is applied per arm only after its 23 slots reconcile: `resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1` is an absolute near-total-failure stop, **not** a ranking or proof of general inferiority. Stage B needs the authenticated Stage A seal and disposition, then a separately frozen disjoint corpus and surviving arms **plus both RelayView arms and standard Pi**, with its own admission, seal and report; the stages cannot be pooled ([`docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md`](agent-harness-evals/docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md), “Screening report and futility disposition,” “Stage B,” and “Reporting, generalization and resource limits”).

sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.name: ls
toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description: Search the web using the current supported provider (Google Gemini, xAI Grok, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Ollama, or OpenCode Zen/Go). Optionally include URLs to analyze alongside search results.

query.description: The search query or question to answer

urls.description: Additional URLs to analyze along with search (up to 20)

toolsAdded.name: web_fetch
toolsAdded.description:
Retrieves and extracts the main content of a web page as markdown.

Include a 'prompt' parameter to have an LLM distill the page down to just the information you need — this saves significant context compared to ingesting raw page content.
Without a prompt, the full extracted markdown is returned (or a structured overview if the page is large).

Batch mode: use 'pages' instead of 'url' to fetch multiple URLs in a single call. Each entry can have its own prompt.
This is much faster than making separate web_fetch calls when you need content from several pages.
The 'url' and 'pages' parameters are mutually exclusive. Maximum 10 pages per batch.

When to use something else:
- The gh CLI (via bash) for anything on GitHub — issues, PRs, repo contents, API calls.

Behavior notes:
- URLs must include the scheme (e.g. https://). Plain HTTP is silently upgraded to HTTPS.
- Fetched content is held in a short-lived cache, so asking multiple questions about the same page is cheap.
- Cross-host redirects are surfaced rather than followed — make a second request to the target URL.
- No files or external state are modified by this tool.

url.description: Fully-formed URL to fetch (e.g., https://example.com/page). Mutually exclusive with 'pages'.

prompt.description: What information to extract from the page. Strongly recommended — the page content will be processed by a fast LLM and only relevant information returned. Omit only if you need the full raw content. Only used with 'url', not 'pages'.
What information to extract from this page

pages.description: Array of pages to fetch concurrently (max 10). Mutually exclusive with 'url'. Each entry can have its own prompt.

# Agent Harness Evaluations

Local coding-agent comparisons using pinned [Inspect AI](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/).
Inspect owns evaluation execution, Docker sandbox lifecycle, scoring and logs.
The repository supplies native-product adapters, research/account policy,
independent task verification and experiment definitions.

The current benchmark is the [staged MultiLang v5 contract](docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md):
a 25-task, seven-arm Stage A, followed by a separately frozen Stage B with
surviving standard arms, Pi and RelayView. See the [delivery roadmap](docs/contracts/unified-benchmark-roadmap.md).
A complete comparative Stage A has not yet been published.

## Current execution

Five-project operational qualification and Stage A share
`stage_a_execution.execute_attempt`: native execution, sanitized task preparation,
terminal candidate capture, quiescence, independent verification, retained Inspect
evidence and task-outcome-v2 normalization. Task-specific verification differs:
SWE-bench's five Python projects use their pinned commands/parser; MultiLang uses
its pinned language-specific commands and separate parser environment.

- [Current five-project qualification and retirement guide](docs/runbooks/current-qualification.md)
